rationale: Trace how a restarted node re-establishes its configuration ('context validity') when the committed-log replay feature is enabled. NewRaft replays committed logs first (restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index) and then scans the log for configuration entries starting at max(lastSnapshot, lastApplied)+1. Because the scan is skipped over the committed prefix, configuration entries inside it are never applied to r.configurations when no snapshot carries them, even though they remain in the log. Focused probe: restart a single-voter node that was bootstrapped and applied commands but never snapshotted, with RestoreCommittedLogs on/off and with a covering snapshot as control.

investigations.question: Does a node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, whose newest configuration entry is inside the persisted commit index and has no covering snapshot, still know that configuration after NewRaft returns?
investigations.hypothesis: No. restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so the configuration scan starts after the committed prefix and never calls processConfigurationLogEntry for the configuration entry that only exists in the log. r.configurations.latest stays empty (or stays at the snapshot configuration), so the node loses its own membership context, cannot start elections, and skips the membership checks when granting votes.
investigations.discriminator: Restart the same durable state twice: with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and with RestoreCommittedLogs=false. Predict servers_after=0 and no re-election with the feature on, versus servers_after=1 and a successful re-election with it off. A third run takes a snapshot before restart to show that a snapshot-carried configuration masks the loss (servers_after=1), separating the scanning bound from generic restart damage.

gaps.question: Can the silently-created two-server change ({A,B,C} -> {A,B,E}, committed with A plus a promoted caught-up nonvoter E while B is partitioned) let the old majority {B,C} elect a leader in a higher term that then truncates A's committed entry X when the partition heals, and can the two sides therefore hold leaders of different terms over the same log?

interpretations.rationale: Three independent receipts, all retained. (1) 430d7ba602ed4666bdfe63a96c71e2fc index 1: with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and no snapshot the restarting node returns with an empty configuration (servers_after=0 against servers_before=1), never campaigns again in a 3s opportunity, and logs 'no known peers, aborting election'; both the non-replay run (index 3) and the snapshot run (index 5) keep the configuration and re-elect. (2) d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740 index 1: with a snapshot carrying {A,B}@1 and a committed AddVoter C at index 8 with staged commit 11, the restarted node reports 2 servers while its continuously running peer reports 3 and its own log still holds the newest configuration entry; index 3: a later AddVoter E then returns no error and both nodes converge on 3 members without C (contains_c_final=false), i.e. a legitimately added voter is silently removed from the cluster by a change computed from the stale base. (3) edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d index 1: the isolated control with RestoreCommittedLogs=false scores holds (servers_after=1 against the same bootstrapped voter), so the replayed committed prefix, not restart itself, is the cause. (4) 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a index 1: restarting all three voters at once with the flag leaves servers_after=[0,0,0] and nodes_with_full_config=0 with no leader in a six-second opportunity, while the same procedure without the flag scores holds at index 3 (nodes_with_full_config=3, leader elected) - a cluster-wide progress loss, not a single node's lost context. (5) 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837: with only two of three voters restarted, the untouched configured voter leads with the configuration-less nodes' votes (index 0, servers_after=[0,0,3]); once that voter stops, the two remaining live, fully up-to-date voters cannot elect a leader in six seconds at 50ms timeouts (index 1, log last index 13 on both), while the control without the flag re-elects immediately (index 3). Source chain: restoreFromCommittedLogs raises lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 723-755); the configuration scan then begins at max(lastSnapshot,lastApplied)+1 (api.go 611-613), so configuration entries inside the committed prefix are never fed to their only producer processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1605-1623) unless a snapshot carries them (api.go 645-689). With Servers empty the follower refuses to campaign (raft.go 230-234 on every heartbeat timeout, raft.go 214-251) and both vote handlers skip their membership checks (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784); with Servers stale, appendConfigurationEntry derives the next membership from that stale base (raft.go 1204-1241, configuration.go 224-302) once the admission gate sees latest==committed (raft.go 654-664). (6) 79d93a5aaad448888cc04214be8f2ad8: with A's configuration coming from a snapshot ({A,B}) while its log holds the newer {A,B,C} entry, AddVoter E returned no error and the silently created two-server change committed at index 11 with A's commit index at 11 and E holding the same LogConfiguration entry (parsed index 2), while B stayed at log index 10 with the old membership; the old majority {B,C} then elected B in term 4 while A was still leader in term 3 (parsed index 3, a_still_leader=true), and after the partition healed A's entry 11 was a LogNoop of term 4 rather than the committed configuration entry (parsed index 4, committed_entry_truncated=true).
counterevidence: The isolated control receipt edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d scores holds with the identical restart and no snapshot (servers_after=1), so the loss is caused by replaying the committed prefix, not by restart, snapshot absence, or the commit-tracking store.

The snapshot run inside the first receipt (index 5) keeps the configuration, so the defect requires the newest configuration entry to be inside the skipped prefix; a snapshot taken after the change masks it.
Voter C never runs in the two-voter probe, so nothing in the receipts shows C resisting or noticing its removal; the claim is about the configuration the running nodes decide with.

The cluster-wide receipt 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a scores the control comparison holds (index 3, nodes_with_full_config=3) and the failing case violated (index 1, nodes_with_full_config=0), so the empty configuration after a simultaneous restart is specific to the replayed committed prefix.

Receipt 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837 scores the control comparison holds (index 3: the two live voters re-elect a leader without the flag) and the failing case violated (index 1: after the configured voter stops, no leader among the two live voters although both hold every committed entry, log last index 13 on both), so the loss of electability is tied to the missing configuration rather than to the restart or the shutdown.

The dual-majority path needs a caught-up nonvoter E so the silent change can commit without the partitioned voter B; without such a node the change would need B's acknowledgement and B would then hold the new membership.
limitations: All executions are in-process in-memory clusters at protocol version 3 with 50ms heartbeat/election timeouts and a single committed configuration change; joint-consensus or multi-step changes are not exercised.

The multi-node progress consequence (a live quorum of up-to-date voters unable to elect after the configured voter stops) is the subject of the partial-restart experiment requested in this update; the authority consequence that configuration-less nodes still grant votes is observed indirectly there (the configured voter wins their votes) and read from source (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784).
The finding is specific to RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; with the flag disabled the same durable state recovers normally in every receipt.

The configuration-less nodes still act as voters in other respects (they granted the configured voter's election win in receipt 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837, index 0), which is why the cluster survived until that voter stopped; this is read from the receipt and from the membership checks being skipped for an empty configuration (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784).

In that probe the partitioned side elects its leader with 3s election timeouts (reloaded to keep the restarted leader from losing the first election), so the interval is seconds; the ordering it demonstrates does not depend on those particular values.

Receipt 79d93a5aaad448888cc04214be8f2ad8 reproduced all dual-majority observations but scored both comparisons unknown because the declared identity field was missing from the result events; those observations are cited as parsed indices rather than as scored comparisons, and the corrected successor experiment is requested in this update.

The dual-majority probe has no control variant: with the flag disabled the leader's configuration is current, so the same AddVoter is a single-server change and cannot create disjoint majorities (nextConfiguration over the current configuration, configuration.go 224-302).
interpretations.joint_history: All receipts belong to this question and were executed from the same snapshot. 430d7ba6 (empty configuration), d2d1cb09 (stale configuration and the silently dropped voter), edfd3c20 (isolated control, holds), 4f4a771f (all voters restart, cluster-wide progress loss), 7afe8c04 (live quorum cannot elect) and 79d93a5a (silent two-server change, concurrent leaders, truncation of the committed entry) form one chain: each was built from the previous receipt's outcome, and each uses the same bootstrap/commit/snapshot/restart operations rather than fabricated state.

9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3-gap-0.explanation: Resolved by retained receipt d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740: the restarted node adopts the snapshot-carried configuration when the newest configuration entry lies inside the replayed committed prefix (comparison 0 violated, witness index 1: servers_after=2 while the peer reports 3 and the newest configuration entry index 8 is below the staged commit index 11), and that stale base changes a real decision (comparison 2 violated, witness index 3: AddVoter E returned no error and both nodes ended with 3 members and contains_c_final=false, so voter C was silently removed). The same receipt's control mode kept 3 members and ended with 4 including C (observed at parsed index 5; that comparison was scored unknown because both modes shared a result event name, which the dedicated control experiment has now replaced with a scored holds).

a8b8d696ac934beda1434a93b5d7758f-gap-1.explanation: Partly answered by source and receipt trace, not yet executed. The obvious route cannot work: a voter that never receives the silently-created {A,B,E} entry is strictly behind in the log, and the log up-to-date check in requestVote/requestPreVote (raft.go 1731-1746, 1812-1828) makes any voter that holds the entry refuse to vote for it, so the removed voter C cannot win alone or with a lagging peer. A disjoint-majority election therefore needs a majority of the OLD configuration whose members all lack the entry, which means the entry must commit without one of the old voters acking it. That is reachable because appendConfigurationEntry installs the new configuration into the commitment immediately on append (raft.go 1238-1240), so {A,B,E} commits with A plus a promoted, already-caught-up nonvoter E, without B. The remaining question is whether the partitioned old voter B can then be elected by the old majority {B,C} in a higher term and truncate A's committed entry X when the partition heals (appendEntries clears the conflicting suffix, raft.go 1541-1552), which would lose a committed entry. Requirements identified: a stale-config leader A that keeps leadership long enough, a caught-up nonvoter E (so the change commits without B), B partitioned for the change, and healing afterwards so the higher-term leader's appendEntries reaches A. The next experiment is designed to that discriminator.

1ed9540f22fe4fa9bef3b3bda88e22e8-gap-2.explanation: Resolved by retained receipt 79d93a5aaad448888cc04214be8f2ad8: the silent two-server change {A,B,C} -> {A,B,E} committed on A plus the promoted caught-up nonvoter E (parsed index 2: change_err nil, x_index 11, committed=true, entry type LogConfiguration on A and on E, A commit index 11, B still at log index 10); the old majority {B,C} elected B in term 4 while A was still leader in term 3 (parsed index 3), i.e. two concurrent leaders with disjoint support over the same log; and after healing, A's entry at index 11 became a LogNoop of term 4 (parsed index 4), so the entry committed under the configuration recorded in the logs was truncated on the node that had committed it. The receipt's own comparison scoring failed because of my identity wiring (x_index was not emitted in the result events), which the successor experiment in this update corrects.

scope.description: Four in-process nodes at protocol version 3 with 300ms heartbeat/election/lease: A and B are bootstrapped as voters {A,B}; A snapshots, adds E as a caught-up nonvoter, adds C as a voter (config {A,B,C} plus nonvoter E), commits four commands. A is shut down and restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs=true so its in-memory configuration comes from the snapshot ({A,B}) while its log holds the newer {A,B,C} entry; the other three nodes get longer timeouts so the restarted leader wins back leadership. B is then partitioned from A (C is already absent from A's stale configuration, so A replicates to nobody but E), and A issues one AddVoter E. Observations: whether that change commits and with whose acknowledgement, each side's configuration and log tail, who leads each side and in which term, and the content of A's log at the created entry index before and after the partition is healed.
assumptions: E is a caught-up nonvoter before the change, which is what lets the silently-created {A,B,E} configuration commit with A and E alone once B is partitioned; this is ordinary use of AddNonvoter followed by AddVoter.
Restarting the leader with RestoreCommittedLogs=true is the documented configuration already established by the earlier receipts; nothing else about the cluster changes.
The partition is applied by disconnecting the in-memory transports in both directions, which is a real partition for all Raft traffic (AppendEntries, heartbeats, votes).
Both sides keep following the protocol: A leads the {A,B,E} configuration with E's acknowledgements, and B and C campaign under their own {A,B,C} configuration after their election timeout.
excluded: No control variant: with the flag disabled the leader's configuration is current, so the same AddVoter adds a single server and the two-server change cannot arise; that is a source-level statement (nextConfiguration over the current configuration) rather than an execution.
No disk faults or message loss; the only partition is the one applied explicitly.

experiment.prefix: Real bootstrap, real snapshot, real AddNonvoter catch-up, real AddVoter, real commits, graceful shutdown and restart of the leader on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore instances, real transport partition and real healing. The log, snapshot metadata and configurations all come from those operations; the harness never fabricates entries or configuration state.

comparisons.description: An entry committed under the configuration recorded in the logs must not be replaced after the partition heals.
At most one leader may exist for a given log: the old-configuration side must not elect a leader while the new-configuration side still leads.

experiment.revision_reason: The executed run reproduced every observation but both comparisons were scored unknown because the identity field I declared (x_index) was absent from the result events and the prerequisite event could therefore not be correlated to them. The harness now emits x_index in old_side_elected and after_heal, so the admission on silent_change (committed, entry_type_at_x=LogConfiguration) correlates with both result events; predictions, scope and prefix are unchanged, and the corrected harness was re-verified in an isolated copy of the captured tree.

knowledge.statement: NewRaft does not restore a configuration entry that lies inside the replayed committed log prefix: with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled the configuration comes only from the newest snapshot plus configuration entries above max(lastSnapshot, persistedCommitIndex), so a node restarted from a log whose newest configuration entry is at or below the persisted commit index adopts the snapshot configuration (empty when there is no snapshot) instead of the replicated one.
knowledge.conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true; LogStore implements CommitTrackingLogStore; node started on stores whose persisted commit index is at or above the newest configuration entry index; no snapshot whose ConfigurationIndex covers that entry.
